title: Catfish Pepper Soup
author: Ronke Adeyemi
desc: A whole catfish, two cups of stock, a teaspoon of pepper soup spice and a pinch of utazi — covered and simmered twenty-five minutes, and that is the whole recipe.
longDesc: This is the simplest serious dish in the collection: everything goes into the pot at once, the lid goes on, and twenty-five minutes later it is done. A whole catfish cut and cleaned, two cups of stock or water, a teaspoon of pepper soup spice, a bouillon cube, a tablespoon of oil, salt, and a pinch of utazi or bitter leaf. No frying, no stages, no stirring. Note that the spice blend's components are named on the page but not proportioned, so the teaspoon is not reproducible from the page alone — for a blend with actual proportions see NGA078.
ingredients: A pinch of utazi or bitter leaf
steps: Clean the catfish and cut it into steaks. Pour hot water over the pieces to remove the slime, then rinse in cold water.
Place the cleaned fish in a pot with the stock or water.
Add the pepper soup mix, the salt, the bouillon cube, the oil and the utazi.
chefTips: Hot water over the catfish first to deal with the slime, then cold water to rinse. Skip it and the broth will be cloudy and faintly muddy.
Cut into steaks, not chunks. Catfish holds together in rounds and falls apart in cubes.
Cover it and leave it. Twenty-five minutes without stirring — this is a dish you can ignore.
A pinch of utazi, no more. It is bitter and it is there as a counterweight to the richness of the fish.
Two cups of stock to one fish gives you a proper brothy pepper soup. Reduce it if you want something closer to a sauce.

The page lists the spice blend's components — allspice seed, anise pepper, cloves, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, dried ginger, fennel seeds, tamarind pulp and ground pepper — but gives no proportions, so the teaspoon is not reproducible from that page. Use the proportioned blend at NGA078, or a commercial mix.
Point and kill is what this is called when the fish is chosen live from a tank at a roadside bar. It is as fresh as Nigerian cooking gets.
commonMistakes: Cutting the fish into small chunks.
Using more than a pinch of utazi.
Expecting to reproduce the spice blend from this page's component list.
sources: Adapted from 'Catfish Pepper Soup', byline 'By Ronke Edoho', 9jafoodie — one of the few pages on that site carrying a personal byline. Quantities as printed: 1 whole catfish cut and cleaned; 1 teaspoon peppersoup spice mix; 1 tablespoon oil of choice; 1 cube maggi; salt; 2 cups stock or water; utazi or bitter leaf (a pinch). Method as printed: place the cleaned fish in a pot with stock or water; add the pepper soup mix, salt, maggi, oil and utazi; 'cover and simmer for 25 minutes'. Yield not specified.

FLAGGED: the headnote describes the spice blend as allspice seed, anise pepper, cloves, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, dried ginger, fennel seeds, tamarind pulp and ground pepper — but gives NO PROPORTIONS, so the '1 teaspoon peppersoup spice mix' is not reproducible from this page. For a pepper soup spice blend with actual stated proportions, see NGA078.

The slime-removal step is from the same author's Nupe catfish stew (NGA103), where it is given as: pour hot water over the pieces to remove slime, rinse in cold water and pat dry. It is applied here because the same cleaning problem applies.

PLACEMENT NOTE: this page presents the dish as generically Nigerian rather than specifically Niger Delta, so it is filed as National. Pepper soup is genuinely pan-Nigerian — the Urhobo version with its own spice names is at NGA078 and the Urhobo yam pottage built on the same base is at NGA047.
reheating: Low heat. The fish will soften further.
healthBenefits: Catfish is a lean source of protein and omega-3 fats.
Very low in carbohydrate and calories.
Pepper soup spices are traditionally used as digestives and decongestants.
Utazi is used for digestion and blood sugar.
culturalNote: Point and kill is the name for this at a roadside bar: you pick your catfish live from a tank and it is in a bowl of pepper soup twenty-five minutes later. Pepper soup generally is Nigeria's restorative — eaten when someone has a cold, after childbirth, late at night with a drink — and the catfish version is the one most associated with the Delta and the rivers.
